p: Jesus being full of the Holy: Christ, being carried away (as it were out of the world) into the desert, comes suddenly as if from heaven, having fasted for forty days and overcoming Satan three times, and thus begins his office.

And the devil said unto him: Christ, being tempted by Satan, first to distrust in God, secondly to the desire of riches and honour, and lastly to a vain confidence in himself, overcomes him three times by the word of God.
power will I give thee: By this word "power" are meant the kingdoms themselves which have the power: and so this is said using the figure of speech metonymy.

delivered unto me: This is surely so, for he is prince of the world, but not absolutely, and is the sovereign of it only by permission and request, and therefore he does not truly say that he can give it to whom he will.
thine: Out of a high place, from which would be seen a good and first-class country, and thus the devil showed him all countries.
And he came to Nazareth: Who Christ is and for what reason he came he shows from the prophet Isaiah.
opened the book: Their books in those days were rolled up as scrolls upon a ruler: and so Christ unrolled or unfolded it, which is here called "opened".
And all: Familiarity causes Christ to be condemned and therefore he often goes to strangers.

bare him witness: Approved those things which he spoke with common consent and voice: for this word "witness" signifies in this place (and many others) "to allow and approve a thing with open confession".

wondered at the: Present at this meeting of the scriptures were not only the learned, but also the common people: and besides that, their mother tongue was used, for how else could the people have wondered? Paul appointed the same manner for doing things in the Church at Corinth; 1Co 14:1-40.

gracious words which proceeded out of: Words full of the mighty power of God, which appeared in all his doings, and as well allured men marvellously unto him; see Ps 45:2, "grace is poured into thy lips".
land: Land of Israel; see Geneva
And all they in the synagogue: The more sharply the world is rebuked the more it openly rages: but the life of the godly is not always subject to the desires of the wicked.
Saying: Christ astonishes not only men, be they ever so stupid, but even the demons as well, whether or not they want to be.
And he arose out of the: In that Christ heals the diseases of the body with only his word, he proves that he is God Almighty, sent for man's salvation.
And devils also came out of: Satan, who is a continual enemy of the truth, ought not to be heard, not even when he speaks the truth.
And when it was day: No zealous response on the part of the people ought to hinder us in the race that God has appointed unto us.
